threads.body: `record_stream_chunk()` can still record streaming timing metrics (and mutate timing state) after the invocation has already been finalized via `stop()`/`fail()` because it doesn't check whether the invocation is still active. Since this is a public entry point intended for callback-driven integrations, it should be a no-op once `_finish()` has run to avoid emitting late metric points and leaving span attributes inconsistent (span already ended).
